chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Benny Carter's all-saxophone date: Hawkins outplays Phil Woods on 'Midnight Sun'
summary: On a 1964 Carter date with five saxophones, Hawkins took the solo and amazed Phil Woods by playing the tune every which way.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah, he was. And Ben and Coleman Hawkins. But Hawk now, speaking of this same band, Phil Woods, they featured -- one of his featured numbers in Quincy's band was 'Midnight Sun Never Sets,' you know. What is that, 'the Midnight Sun.'
Yeah, the one that -- no, no.
No, no, the one that Quincy wrote.

Yeah. Beautiful number. And they featured Phil Woods And Phil did a tremendous job on it. Okay? He's a modernist. So I was in New York in later years and Benny Carter was there to do some recording, so he called me to do this recording with him. Good. Now, I guess this was another -- this was a little before supersax, because Benny had the same idea. There was all saxophone. There was a rhythm section and saxophone. They had Phil Woods, Coleman Hawkins, Rouse, I forget his first -- Charlie Rouse, and Bennie Carter, and I forget the others. Five saxophones. So it was all like supersax, you know. Now, this was in the sixties, you know.
They weren't doing someone's solos, though
They did a Coleman Hawkins solo on Body and Soul, yeah.
This was '64. 1964, around that time, because Nat died in '65. It had to be around '64, around this time. But --
And you were on this date?

Yeah, it was on this date, yeah. Joe Jones and the Jimmy Garrison was playing bass. And what's -- that's an interesting story, I'll get to that one in a moment. But Phil Woods as I told you had been playing this number, the Midnight Sun and (inaudible). But Benny on this date gave the solo to Coleman Hawkins. And Phil Woods never heard so much that 'Midnight Sun never Sets' in his life, as Coleman Hawkins played. The old man, the gray old man. You know. He played this tune, he played it sideways, up and down, vertically, horizontally, every way the changes were jumping. It was just beautiful. Phil's mouth flew open when he heard this.
